parsed.headline: Syrian woman killed in Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

pages.text: Buthaina Ahmad Oweida, a 56-year-old Syrian mother of four, was among those killed during a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, according to reporting by Arab News. Oweida, who was originally from the Idlib province of northern Syria, had lived in Saudi Arabia for four years after fleeing the civil war in her homeland. At the time of the attack, she was traveling from Riyadh to her home in Makkah after visiting her sister to assist in caring for an injured nephew. Her sister, Hayat Oweida, told Arab News from Idlib that Buthaina had intended to perform Umrah upon her return. Hayat stated that Buthaina had insisted on traveling despite family concerns regarding a previous attack on the airport. Hayat reported that a phone call between Buthaina and her nephew was suddenly cut off while she was at the airport.

parsed.headline: Legal scholar questions NPP suit regarding presidential term limits in Ghana

pages.text: Legal scholar Kwaku Azar Asare has questioned whether a suit filed by the New Patriotic Party (NPP) at the Supreme Court of Ghana presents a justiciable constitutional dispute or constitutes a request for an advisory opinion. The NPP has filed the suit seeking an interpretation of Article 66(2) of the 1992 Constitution, which mandates a four-year presidential term and limits individuals to two terms in office. Specifically, the party is seeking a declaration that the two-term limit applies regardless of whether the terms are consecutive or non-consecutive. The legal action has drawn attention to the constitutional implications of presidential term limits ahead of the 2028 general election, though the filing does not establish that President John Dramani Mahama intends to seek another term.

In a Facebook post, Mr. Asare argued that the current writ differs from previous constitutional cases pursued by the NPP, such as the 31st December Case and a challenge to police permit requirements for public demonstrations. He noted that those prior cases involved identifiable government actions or existing laws alleged to be inconsistent with the Constitution, whereas the current suit does not identify an allegedly unconstitutional enactment, act, or omission requiring judicial intervention. Mr. Asare stated that no one has filed to contest a third presidential election and no electoral authority has determined that a person elected twice is eligible for a third election. He maintained that a disagreement over the meaning of a constitutional provision does not, by itself, establish a justiciable controversy, suggesting the matter is at best a public debate over what the Constitution permits.

parsed.headline: Africa CDC official warns Ebola outbreak could reach UK

pages.text: Dr. Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), has warned that an unprecedented Ebola outbreak in Africa could reach the United Kingdom and other countries. Kaseya compared the potential spread of the illness to the Covid-19 pandemic, noting that the outbreak has already reached 10,000 cases and almost 5,000 deaths. He stated that countries are not safe unless they take appropriate measures and emphasized that more funding must be secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment to prevent the virus from spreading globally.

parsed.headline: Israeli election results remain uncertain as Ebola infections in Democratic Republic of Congo surpass 10,000

pages.text: The election in Israel is currently too close to call following record voter turnout. Voters are deciding whether to retain Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or replace him with an alternative, including his top rival, Gadi Eisenkot, a center-right former military chief of staff. Because final vote tallies may take time, if no bloc secures a majority, it could take days or weeks for party leaders to form a governing coalition and determine the next prime minister.  In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola outbreak has surpassed 10,000 people infected since it was declared in May, according to the latest government figures. The outbreak is described as the fastest-spreading in history and the largest ever in geographic scope, spanning from Nigeria to Kenya. Katie Thomas-Canfield, interim Ebola response director for the International Rescue Committee, stated that the speed at which the milestone was reached was surprising.

The current Ebola outbreak has a death toll of nearly 5,000, which is second only to the West Africa outbreak of 2014-2016 that saw over 11,000 deaths. Approximately one-third of those who have died in this outbreak are children. Children under 5 are hit especially hard, with roughly three out of every four infected children dying. Mohamed Janabi, regional director for the World Health Organization Africa, noted at a press conference last week that the figures represent lives interrupted and communities seeking reassurance.

parsed.headline: Ghana signs Accra Convention to allow road, rail, and air cargo to serve as loan collateral

pages.text: Ghana has become the first country to sign the Accra Convention, a new global treaty designed to allow goods moving by road, rail, and air to be used as collateral for bank loans. According to Graphic Online, the signing took place during a ceremony in Accra titled the UN Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents (Accra Convention), which also commemorated the 60th anniversary of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL). Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, the Minister of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, signed the convention and described the move as a major boost for African traders whose capital was previously locked up on trucks.

The treaty addresses a gap in transport finance where road, rail, and air transport lack a comparable instrument to the maritime bill of lading. For over a century, the maritime bill of lading has functioned as a document of title, allowing cargo to be pledged to a bank or sold during a voyage through the transfer of the document. In contrast, existing instruments such as the Convention on the Contract for the International Carriage of Goods by Road (CMR), rail consignment notes, and air waybills under the Montreal Convention are deliberately non-negotiable.

parsed.headline: Tanzania announces natural gas discovery in Mnazi Bay area

pages.text: Tanzania has announced its first major natural gas discovery in a decade, with an estimated 223 billion cubic feet found at the Kasa-1X ST2 well in the Mnazi Bay area of the country's south. The well is jointly owned by the state-run Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (TPDC) and the French energy company Maurel & Prom. Energy Minister Juma Homera attended a ceremony at the well to mark the occasion, describing the find as a major milestone for the nation's oil and gas sector. Authorities stated the discovery is intended to help provide reliable, clean, and affordable energy as demand increases due to industrial growth and other economic activities. Production at the well is expected to begin early next month to boost supplies for households, industry, and vehicles. Natural gas already accounts for nearly 80 percent of Tanzania's electricity generation, according to 2024 government statistics. The country holds existing natural gas reserves of 57.54 trillion cubic feet. Previous significant discoveries in the region include finds on Songo Songo Island in 1974 and at Mnazi Bay in 1982, with the largest single discovery of 2.7 trillion cubic feet occurring in 2016.

parsed.headline: Alberta government to pursue independent dental and drug plans following referendum defeat

pages.text: The United Conservative Party (UCP) government in Alberta intends to proceed with plans to opt out of federal dental and drug benefit programs in favor of provincial approaches, despite voters rejecting a related strategy in a recent referendum. The province has been seeking to establish independent paths for the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) and the national pharmacare program since 2024. In the referendum, 57 per cent of voters rejected a UCP proposal to lead a constitutional amendment that would allow provinces to opt out of federal programs while retaining federal funding through a blanket opt-out rule regarding constitutional spending power.

Maddison McKee, press secretary for the Ministry of Hospital and Surgical Health Services, stated that the government will continue to advocate for a fair share of federal funding to strengthen provincial dental and drug programs and will call for predictable, sustainable, and unconditional health funding that respects provincial jurisdiction. While the province previously stated it would pursue an independent path for the CDCP by 2026, McKee did not provide an updated timeline following the referendum. According to federal government data, as of Sept. 30, 349,000 Albertans were enrolled in the CDCP for the 2026-2027 benefit period, with 91,000 having received an approved claim.

parsed.headline: Aiden Pleterski maintains innocence in Toronto fraud trial closing statement

pages.text: Aiden Pleterski, a 27-year-old self-described “Crypto King,” addressed a jury for the first time during his fraud trial in Ontario Superior Court on Wednesday morning. In a brief closing statement, Pleterski thanked the jury and asserted his innocence, stating, “I am innocent of these charges. That is why I pled not guilty. Had I not been forced to represent myself, that would have been proven.” Pleterski, who was charged in May 2024 following a police investigation, has been representing himself at trial. During the proceedings, he cross-examined only the first of 14 Crown witnesses and chose not to testify or present evidence in his defense. When asked by Justice Shaun Nakatsuru if he had questions for witnesses, Pleterski indicated he did not know what to ask and, in one instance, stated he needed a lawyer.

Prior to Pleterski's statement, Crown prosecutor Akshay Aurora delivered a roughly 90-minute closing statement to the jury. Aurora alleged that Pleterski was a “thief” who used “calculated lies” to steal investor money to fund his lifestyle while ignoring investor inquiries. The prosecution's case included testimony from an accountant alleging Pleterski spent $16.3 million of investor funds on items such as jets, cars, security, and credit cards, as well as a recording in which Pleterski allegedly admitted a $300 million fund did not exist. Pleterski is accused of fraud over $5,000. A separate charge of money laundering against him was dropped by the Crown at the conclusion of their case.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh Prime Minister vows to address Japanese firms' business concerns

pages.text: On October 28, 2026, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman assured Japanese companies that his government would address concerns regarding the country's business environment. Speaking at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum Dialogue at the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) headquarters in Tokyo, Rahman identified three key areas of concern raised by Japanese firms: reliable energy, efficient infrastructure, and predictable customs clearance and taxation. He stated that the government has already resolved some issues and is working to address remaining outstanding matters. The forum was organized by JETRO in cooperation with the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation, with support from the Bangladesh Embassy in Japan. Following the signing of the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), Rahman called for stronger trade and investment ties to elevate the relationship between the two nations. He invited Japanese investment in sectors including automotive manufacturing, energy, technology and space, high-speed rail, and logistics, noting that Bangladesh aims to become a global manufacturing hub due to its large domestic market and export potential.

During his visit to Japan on October 28, 2026, Rahman met with Kazuhiko Amakawa, governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), to discuss energy, infrastructure, and information and communication technology. Rahman urged JBIC to open an office in Dhaka to strengthen economic cooperation, to which Amakawa replied he would seriously consider the request. Rahman also met with Tadashi Yanai, the chairman, president, and chief executive officer of Fast Retailing, the parent company of Uniqlo. Regarding the broader business climate, the Prime Minister stated that his government has initiated regulatory reforms intended to attract both domestic and foreign investment.
